name: lcm
desc: Libraries and tools for message passing and data marshalling
why: Lightweight Communications and Marshalling is a neat multicast message-passing system, but it is a library family rather than a visible door into anything strange.

brief.what_it_is: LCM (Lightweight Communications and Marshalling) is a set of libraries and tools for message passing and data marshalling. It provides a publish/subscribe model in which programs send and receive typed messages over UDP multicast. It also includes automatic code generation that turns message type definitions into marshalling and unmarshalling code for several languages. The README lists C, C++, Java, Lua, MATLAB, and Python (3.7 and later) as supported, with C#/.NET and Go marked unmaintained. Tools shipped alongside it include lcm-gen, lcm-logger, lcm-logplayer, lcm-logplayer-gui, and lcm-spy.
brief.why_it_exists: It is aimed at real-time systems where high bandwidth and low latency are critical. The docs say it was originally developed in 2006 for the MIT DARPA Urban Challenge team and has since been used in many robotic and autonomous systems.
brief.how_it_works: Peers communicate directly over UDP multicast, with no central broker or hub and no daemon process. Message types are described in the LCM type specification language, and the lcm-gen generator produces the type-safe marshalling code for each target language. Logging and playback tools record and replay the traffic.
brief.install_notes: The README links to separate install and build instructions pages (Installing LCM, Build Instructions from source) and to a releases page on GitHub. I did not fetch those pages, so I have no verified commands or steps. The docs also list a separate UDP Multicast Setup page, which suggests network configuration may matter for multicast traffic to work. Nothing in the pages I read mentioned special hardware or accounts.
brief.standout: It avoids the usual broker-based design: there is no central database, hub, or daemon, and peers talk to each other directly over multicast. Typed message definitions also generate matching code across several languages, and the logging and playback tools are built in.
brief.status: Maintained, per the GitHub README's Roadmap section, which says "The LCM project is active again" and that the current plan is stability and maintenance patches. I did not see a release date or last-commit date in the pages I fetched, so the recency of activity is unverified beyond that note.
brief.caveats: The README lists Go and C#/.NET as unmaintained, and says PRs are welcome for them. Platform support is listed as GNU/Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04, Fedora 42), macOS 14 and 15, and Windows 2019 and 2022, plus other POSIX-1.2001 systems per the docs. The homepage I first requested redirects to the /lcm/ docs path. I did not check the license.
quotes: LCM is a set of libraries and tools for message passing and data marshalling, targeted at real-time systems where high-bandwidth and low latency are critical.
No centralized "database" or "hub" -- peers communicate directly
The LCM project is active again.
